page: Amazon Web Services c9g.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture using the Neoverse-V3 model, running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core efficiency, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores placing in the top tier. Passmark memory performance also ranks in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core operations, such as Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, fall into the average category. The instance exhibits weak performance in Passmark CPU encryption and overall Passmark CPU scores, placing in the bottom 25 percent. LLM inference capabilities are mixed, showing average speeds for small models but poor prompt processing performance for medium 7B models.

The c9g.xlarge offers a specialized hardware profile where single-threaded compute and memory bandwidth are prioritized over raw multi-core scaling and cryptographic acceleration. The absence of local storage means workloads must rely on network-attached storage options. This instance is suited for single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, lightweight web serving, and software compilation workloads that benefit from high single-core performance and ARMv9 architecture efficiencies.
